answer.short: The sum of the roots gives $u+v=6$, and the triple-product relation gives $-t^2(u+v)=-c$, so $c=6t^2$.
answer.worked:
Sum of roots:
$$\begin{align*}t-t+u+v&=6\\u+v&=6\end{align*}$$
Sum of products three at a time:
$$\begin{align*}-t^2u-t^2v+tuv-tuv&=-c\\-t^2(u+v)&=-c\\-t^2(6)&=-c\\c&=6t^2\end{align*}$$

answer.short: The pair and product relations give $uv=b+t^2$ and $d=-t^2uv$. With $t^2=\dfrac c6$, this gives $36d=-6bc-c^2$, so $c^2+6bc+36d=0$.
answer.worked:
Sum of products two at a time:
$$\begin{align*}-t^2+tu+tv-tu-tv+uv&=b\\uv-t^2&=b\\uv&=b+t^2\end{align*}$$
Product of roots:
$$d=-t^2uv$$
Substitute $uv=b+t^2$ and $t^2=\dfrac c6$ from part a:
$$\begin{align*}d&=-t^2(b+t^2)\\d&=-\frac c6\left(b+\frac c6\right)\\36d&=-6bc-c^2\\c^2+6bc+36d&=0\end{align*}$$

content.prompt: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be the roots of $2x^2-6x+3=0$. Find the quadratic equation whose roots are:

answer.worked:
$\alpha+\beta=3$, $\alpha\beta=\frac32$.

Let the new quadratic be $x^2+\frac ba x+\frac ca=0$.
$$\begin{aligned}\frac1\alpha+\frac1\beta&=-\frac ba\\\frac{\alpha+\beta}{\alpha\beta}&=-\frac ba\\\frac{3}{3/2}&=-\frac ba\\2&=-\frac ba\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}\frac1{\alpha\beta}&=\frac ca\\\frac23&=\frac ca\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}x^2-2x+\frac23&=0\\3x^2-6x+2&=0\end{aligned}$$

$\alpha+\beta=3$, $\alpha\beta=\frac32$.

Let the new quadratic be $x^2+\frac ba x+\frac ca=0$.
$$\begin{aligned}\alpha^2+\beta^2&=-\frac ba\\(\alpha+\beta)^2-2\alpha\beta&=-\frac ba\\3^2-2\left(\frac32\right)&=-\frac ba\\6&=-\frac ba\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}\alpha^2\beta^2&=\frac ca\\\left(\frac32\right)^2&=\frac ca\\\frac94&=\frac ca\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}x^2-6x+\frac94&=0\\4x^2-24x+9&=0\end{aligned}$$

$\alpha+\beta=3$, $\alpha\beta=\frac32$.

Let the new quadratic be $x^2+\frac ba x+\frac ca=0$.
$$\begin{aligned}(\alpha-2)+(\beta-2)&=-\frac ba\\\alpha+\beta-4&=-\frac ba\\-1&=-\frac ba\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}(\alpha-2)(\beta-2)&=\frac ca\\\alpha\beta-2(\alpha+\beta)+4&=\frac ca\\\frac32-6+4&=\frac ca\\-\frac12&=\frac ca\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}x^2+x-\frac12&=0\\2x^2+2x-1&=0\end{aligned}$$

answer.short: $\alpha^2+\beta^2=(-2)^2-2(5)=-6<0$, so the roots cannot both be real.

$$\begin{aligned}\alpha^2+\beta^2&=(\alpha+\beta)^2-2\alpha\beta\\&=(-2)^2-2(5)\\&=-6<0\end{aligned}$$
If both roots were real, $\alpha^2+\beta^2$ would be non-negative. Therefore the equation cannot have two real roots.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
Let $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ be the roots of $x^3+3x^2-6x-2=0$.
Find the cubic equation whose roots are $-2\alpha,-2\beta$ and $-2\gamma$.

answer.worked:
For the original roots,
$$\begin{align*}\alpha+\beta+\gamma&=-3\\\alpha\beta+\alpha\gamma+\beta\gamma&=-6\\\alpha\beta\gamma&=2.\end{align*}$$
For the new roots $-2\alpha,-2\beta,-2\gamma$,
$$\begin{align*}-2(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)&=-2(-3)=6,\\4(\alpha\beta+\alpha\gamma+\beta\gamma)&=4(-6)=-24,\\-8\alpha\beta\gamma&=-8(2)=-16.\end{align*}$$
The required equation is
$$\begin{align*}x^3-6x^2+(-24)x-(-16)&=0\\x^3-6x^2-24x+16&=0.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt:
Let $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ be the roots of $2x^3-4x^2+5x+1=0$.
Find the cubic equation whose roots are $\frac1\alpha,\frac1\beta,\frac1\gamma$.

answer.worked:
For the original roots,
$$\begin{align*}\alpha+\beta+\gamma&=2\\\alpha\beta+\alpha\gamma+\beta\gamma&=\frac52\\\alpha\beta\gamma&=-\frac12.\end{align*}$$
For the new roots $\frac1\alpha,\frac1\beta,\frac1\gamma$,
$$\begin{align*}\frac1\alpha+\frac1\beta+\frac1\gamma&=\frac{\alpha\beta+\alpha\gamma+\beta\gamma}{\alpha\beta\gamma}=\frac{5/2}{-1/2}=-5,\\\frac1{\alpha\beta}+\frac1{\alpha\gamma}+\frac1{\beta\gamma}&=\frac{\alpha+\beta+\gamma}{\alpha\beta\gamma}=\frac{2}{-1/2}=-4,\\\frac1{\alpha\beta\gamma}&=\frac1{-1/2}=-2.\end{align*}$$
The required equation is
$$\begin{align*}x^3-(-5)x^2+(-4)x-(-2)&=0\\x^3+5x^2-4x+2&=0.\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt:
Let $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ be the roots of $x^3-4x+6=0$.
Find the cubic equation whose roots are $\frac1\alpha,\frac1\beta,\frac1\gamma$.

answer.worked:
For the original roots,
$$\begin{align*}\alpha+\beta+\gamma&=0\\\alpha\beta+\alpha\gamma+\beta\gamma&=-4\\\alpha\beta\gamma&=-6.\end{align*}$$
For the new roots $\frac1\alpha,\frac1\beta,\frac1\gamma$,
$$\begin{align*}\frac1\alpha+\frac1\beta+\frac1\gamma&=\frac{-4}{-6}=\frac23,\\\frac1{\alpha\beta}+\frac1{\alpha\gamma}+\frac1{\beta\gamma}&=\frac{0}{-6}=0,\\\frac1{\alpha\beta\gamma}&=\frac1{-6}=-\frac16.\end{align*}$$
The required equation is
$$\begin{align*}x^3-\frac23x^2+0x+\frac16&=0\\\color{#ef6068}{6\times}\left(x^3-\frac23x^2+\frac16\right)&=\color{#ef6068}{6\times}\,0\\6x^3-4x^2+1&=0.\end{align*}$$
